subject: Follow-up: model fit & function-calling evals (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.ai>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & function-calling evals (next steps)

Alex 

Thanks again for the time today  really helpful to see the demo and the end-to-end flow you're trying to achieve. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get a focused eval running: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary use: structured API extraction from customer support tickets (JSON output per ticket, fixed schema).
- Volume: ~10k tickets/month for initial phase; bursty during product releases.
- Latency target: 200-1400ms P95 for single ticket responses.
- Data sensitivity: some tickets contain PII  you noted in-call that data will be redacted before we ingest for the eval.

Recommended evaluation plan (2-week pilot):
1) Models to test (suggested order):
   - redwood-chat-7b-fn (function-calling optimized; strong structured output behaviour)
   - redstone-16b-v2 (balanced quality/cost for longer context)
   - llama3-8b-quant (cost-efficient baseline)
2) Benchmarks to collect: schema compliance (% of responses matching JSON schema), mean time-to-first-token, tokens-per-response & cost, retry/failure rate for validation errors.
3) Prompt set: I attached a representative prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.json) containing 200 sample tickets and expected schema examples.
4) Quality regression checks: we will run the samples through a golden-eval harness and surface any regressions vs. your expected outputs; if we see >5% drop in schema compliance we’ll flag for prompt/model adjustments.

Function-calling / JSON schema specifics:
- We can run strict schema enforcement (RPC-style function calls where the model must return JSON matching schema) or a soft enforcement mode where the model returns text + a schema validator step.
- For strict mode, we recommend configuring retries=2 with exponential backoff and deterministic sampling (to reduce nondeterministic failures). If a strict-mode response fails validation after retries, Redwood can: 1) surface the failure to your audit log and 2) optionally send the fallback text variant for downstream parsing.

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm the attached prompt set is representative and that the data will be redacted for the eval.
- If yes, we’ll kick off a smoke test (single-model, 50-sample run) within 48 hours and then the full 2-week run.
- Proposed kickoff: Thu Jul 23 or Fri Jul 24  I’ll block both tentatively; tell me what works for you.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (application/json)

Thanks  I’ll loop Rishi on the procurement/po path once you’re ready to move beyond the eval.

 
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & function-calling evals (next steps)

Alex 

Great  glad to hear PII will be redacted. Quick answers to your questions and a bit more detail on observability/costs: 

Retries & failed payloads:
- Default recommendation: strict schema enforcement with retries=2 (exponential backoff, 200ms -> 500ms).
- If a response fails schema validation after retries we: 1) mark the request as a validation failure, 2) persist the raw model response + the failed parsed payload to the audit logs (redacted where required), and 3) surface the failure in the Redwood Console with a stack trace for the validation step.
- Audit logs are accessible via the Console (role-based access) and can be streamed to your S3/GCS bucket or to a SIEM (we can provide an example infra policy).

Cost / infra options for the eval:
- Hosted sandbox (fastest to start): lower setup friction; good for 2-week pilots. Estimated cost (rough): 
   - redwood-chat-7b-fn: ~$350–550 for the pilot (depends on sample token lengths)
   - redstone-16b-v2: ~$1,200–1,800
   - llama3-8b-quant: ~$180–300
- Dedicated canary: if you want fully consistent latency and isolated capacity we can run the pilot on a small dedicated pool (adds a setup time ~2 business days, and a fixed minimal monthly commit  I’ll have Rishi follow up with exact numbers if you prefer this path).

Attachments included: redwood_benchmark_results_qc.pdf (PDF), acme_prompt_set_v1.json (JSON)  benchmark doc has our baseline schema-compliance results on similar ticket datasets. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-benchmark-acme

If that looks good I’ll schedule the smoke test and we’ll loop Rishi for procurement details (if you want Dedicated).

 
Marissa Cole
